start_here: Say to your AI: "Pin the 5 frames in clip/manifest.json by file identity and tile them into labelled review pages, 2 frames a page." It runs tool:pin-video-frames-as-evidence-pages.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a frame manifest and writes a projection and page images into folders you name.
instructions: 1. Extract frames from your video with your own tool and have a manifest: {"source": {"path"}, "frames": [{"index", "pts", "seconds", "path"}]}. Paths may be relative to the manifest. Pillow must be installed for pages.
2. Have a schema file whose frame_evidence profile names the projection schema (the projection command needs it; frame-pages needs neither schema nor library).

3. Say to your AI: "Pin these frames". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library <library> --schema <schema> project-frame-manifest --manifest clip/manifest.json --output clip/projection.json

4. Then python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library <library> --schema <schema> frame-pages clip/manifest.json clip/pages --per-page 2 --tile-width 160 --quality 40 (add --candidate-pairs to pair adjacent candidate frames).
5. Look at the page images and cite frames by the frame number and time written on them. A page is generated, not reviewed: its index says generated_not_reviewed.

worked_examples.title: Five frames pinned and tiled into three labelled pages
worked_examples.ask: Pin these 5 frames and make review pages of 2.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/read-data/frame_evidence.py and run for real: clip/manifest.json lists 5 made-up 64x36 frames (index 0 to 4, pts 0, 1001, 2002, 3003, 4004 at time base 1/24000), source.mp4 of 19 bytes and change_candidates 1, 2, 3 (the shape test/test_frame_evidence.py uses); clip/schema.json holds the frame_evidence profile from that test. python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library clip --schema clip/schema.json project-frame-manifest --manifest clip/manifest.json --output clip/projection.json; then python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library clip --schema clip/schema.json frame-pages clip/manifest.json clip/pages --per-page 2 --tile-width 160 --quality 40
worked_examples.hands_back: project-frame-manifest exit 0: {"output": ".../clip/projection.json", "frame_count": 5, "source_identity": {"algorithm": "blake3", "bytes": 19, ...}, "manifest_identity": {"algorithm": "blake3", ...}}; projection.json has schema "frames-blake3/v1" and 5 frames each with index, pts, seconds, path, bytes and identity. frame-pages exit 0: {"frame_count": 5, "page_count": 3, "review_status": "generated_not_reviewed"} and clip/pages holds index.json, page-001.jpg, page-002.jpg, page-003.jpg. With --candidate-pairs --pairs-per-page 2 it answers {"pair_count": 3, "page_count": 2, ...} and writes pair-page-001.jpg and pair-page-002.jpg.
